title: Opportunities and constraints

blocks.heading: Opportunities and constraints
blocks.text: Global connections can expand markets, finance and knowledge while exposing producers to competition, shocks and unequal bargaining. Judge participation, local retention, capacity and environmental effects. An increased flow is not by itself proof of a net local benefit.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Opportunities
blocks.text:
Access to larger markets, suitable investment and knowledge can support productive activity. Benefits require the ability to meet quality and delivery needs and opportunities for local workers or suppliers to participate.

Applied example: Access to foreign buyers can expand a producer’s market. International links can supply technology or knowledge that improves productive capability.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Constraints
blocks.text:
Infrastructure gaps, missing skills, finance barriers or dependence on dominant buyers can limit global participation. External competition can challenge local firms while widening consumer options; compare who gains and loses under the stated conditions.

Applied example: Stronger foreign competition can displace producers unable to match price or quality. Reliance on external buyers can expose local work to distant demand shocks.

blocks.heading: Use the evidence
blocks.text: Explain which fictional global-production offer better fits retained local livelihoods. A offers 100 local production jobs with limited training and uses some local suppliers. B offers 60 jobs, more advanced training and more local purchasing, but lower initial output. Both are funded and have buyers. A offers more immediate employment and a genuine local-supply link, which can support more households now. B develops deeper capabilities and retains more supplier spending, but creates fewer jobs initially. Prefer B where lasting skills and stronger local production links are the main priority; A may fit urgent broad employment needs better. Compare job quality, retained spending and future opportunities rather than treating larger output or a foreign connection as proof of local benefit.
